summary: Allwork.Space republishes a Reuters report on a World Health Organization warning about a global medical workforce gap in the 2030s. Drawing on a major WHO report covering workforce trends across more than 100 countries, the statement says populations and health workers are aging simultaneously in many countries, which could intensify a projected global shortage of 11.1 million health workers by 2030. Roughly a quarter of doctors worldwide are expected to retire in the next decade. By 2030, 67 countries are projected to lack the staffing needed to maintain the standards of medical treatment they currently provide. The WHO estimates an additional 832,000 health workers are required simply to hold the current ratio of medical staff to population. The report cautions that shortfalls could drive greater reliance on foreign healthcare workers, drawing staff away from poorer countries and potentially degrading healthcare standards there. Higher income countries, including many in Europe, are expected to be hit hardest because they have a larger share of older healthcare workers; in those countries one in three doctors will retire within ten years. Reporting is credited to Emma Farge with editing by Linda Pasquini. The piece contains no discussion of workplace technology, hybrid work policy, visitor management, desk or room booking, workplace analytics, or facilities operations, and offers no vendor or category language relevant to those areas. It is a general labor market and demographics news item carried by a flexible work publication rather than coverage of workplace tooling or return to office practice.
